a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new field test, operating change or retrofit.
data_requests.how: Establish steam service first: a PRV/PCV or HP/MP/LP/header label alone does not prove steam or two-sided physical topology. Known nonsteam service is not applicable to this steam-turbine question; acknowledge that without a compulsory steam measurement. Missing/unknown data remains qualified. Review existing suitable function before proposing further study.

data_requests.how: The DOE Tip20 source screening figures (3000lb/hr and100psi) describe when to consider further study in its stated context, not automatic install/close thresholds. Do not close an unresolved investigation because data are variable, below an example, unconverted or absent. A backpressure turbine is generally considered in parallel with a PRV and removes energy needed downstream; source prices, graph assumptions/efficiencies and installation percentages are historical examples, not current site savings. Acknowledge an existing suitable function without new measurements or replacement.

questions.decision_rule: Review actual named-station steam service, current balance/flow-duration, process pressure/heat, boiler, electrical and economic constraints before any backpressure-generation feasibility decision. Do not install a turbine or automatically close an unresolved investigation from source thresholds, design pressures or a label alone. Known nonsteam scope can be acknowledged as not applicable; unknown source, association or operating basis remains explicit. No site benefit or operating authorization is calculated.

typical_benefit.wording: Consider when a PRV has "constant steam flows of at least 3,000 pounds per hour (lb/hr), and when the steam pressure drop is at least 100 psi." Installation costs "typically average 75% of equipment costs".
source_titles: S6: Steam Tip #20, Replace Pressure-Reducing Valves with Backpressure Turbogenerators (DOE/GO-102012-3409)

questions.limits: S6 also quotes cost per kW figures; they are deliberately not repeated here. No IAC code maps to turbines (2.2134 covers PRV-station leaks). Source review: complete S6 pp1–2 includes current steam balance/actual process requirements, parallel arrangement, downstream heat/boiler-throughput implications and historical calculation assumptions. Inherited source threshold/cost quotation is not a universal cutoff, present-day quotation or engineering approval.
